hypotheses.title: Routing/cascades/policies schema for dream-mode hypothesis registry
hypotheses.question: Does the routing/cascades/policies schema (primary_anchors, semantic_domain, drift_tolerance; on_drift_timeout / on_arousal / on_lucidity_detected cascade targets; intervention_intensity + require_debounce / allowed_tones policy block; global max_interventions_per_rem_cycle + global_cooldown_seconds + abort_on_repeated_arousal + arousal_threshold_count) capture the relevant design degrees of freedom without bloating into a free-form config?
hypotheses.metric: Schema expressiveness vs current set of 2 example hypotheses (hyp_fear_failure_01, hyp_safe_exploration_01); can the schema represent the brief's D6 safety requirements (60 dB SPL cap, max 5 TMR cues/night, 15-min minimum interval, max 2 hypnopompic wake attempts, sustained-wake abort at 2.5 min, 100ms abort path, battery/thermal/disk preflight) without per-hypothesis ad-hoc fields?
hypotheses.success_criterion: All D6 safety constraints are representable as either global_policies (shared across hypotheses) or per-hypothesis policies (where the constraint is hypothesis-specific, e.g., intervention_intensity:low forbids 'Assertive, grounding' tone for trauma-related hypotheses).
hypotheses.status_note: Schema reviewed 2026-07-19 against the existing Stage 3.4/3.5 hypothesis_registry.json conventions. Conforms to the same shape (id, title, question, metric, success_criterion, expected_effect_size, status, status_note). The routing/cascades/policies blocks extend the schema with three new optional fields; the existing stage_3_4 and stage_3_5 entries are unaffected. Pre-registration is a schema review, not an evidence gate; the hypothesis is registered as a design input, not as a testable empirical claim.

hypotheses.title: Python offline dream-report extraction with human-rated drift baseline
hypotheses.question: Does the three-pass extraction pipeline (denoise -> symbol identification -> analogical mapping) produce drift scores that correlate with human raters' judgments of dream-target alignment, at a level sufficient to use drift as a cascade trigger?
hypotheses.metric: Spearman correlation between LLM-self-evaluated drift_score and human-rater alignment rating on a held-out set of N>=30 dream reports (per D8 H4: 'non-trivial agreement with human raters')
hypotheses.success_criterion: Spearman rho >= 0.5 (medium correlation); F1 of high-drift/low-drift binary classification (threshold = drift_tolerance per hypothesis) >= 0.7

expected_effect_size.spearman_rho: 0.4-0.7 (LLM self-eval is a known weak point; medium correlation is plausible, high is unlikely)

hypotheses.status_note: LLM self-evaluated drift_score is a known weak point for models under 30B parameters. The pipeline must validate against a human-rated baseline before drift can be used as a cascade trigger; otherwise it is an unvalidated heuristic. Synthetic dream reports can be used to test the pipeline extraction end-to-end (denoise + symbol identification + mapping), but the drift-vs-rater correlation requires real labeled data. Candidate LLM: qwen2.5-0.5b per decision_registry.md entry 2; inference via local OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM / MLX-Server / Ollama), not the in-process MLX runtime. Brief's Risk Register: 'LLM primer generation' is Medium status; 'LLM dream report analogy extraction' is Low status. Stage 3.5 = offline evaluation only; no production change.

hypotheses.title: Random Forest 4-class sleep-stage classifier on synthetic 30s EEG epochs
hypotheses.question: Does a Random Forest on relative band power (delta/theta/alpha/beta) achieve cross-subject macro F1 >= 0.6 on a 4-class (Wake, N1, N2_N3, REM) synthetic dataset that mimics Muse's 4-channel frontal derivation?
hypotheses.metric: Macro F1, per-class sensitivity/specificity, Cohen's kappa on LOSO-style splits (synthetic, but with per-subject channel noise injected to simulate cross-subject variability)
hypotheses.success_criterion: Macro F1 >= 0.6 across 4 classes on synthetic; Cohen's kappa >= 0.5

expected_effect_size.feature_count: 4 (relative band powers); brief-flagged as below the literature floor for cross-subject generalization, may need expansion to relative+absolute band powers + theta/alpha ratio + alpha dropout ratio + spindle/slow wave counts (D1 SleepFeatures)

hypotheses.status_note: No labeled sleep-staging dataset exists in the repo. Recordings/ contains Muse validation (eyes-open/closed alpha, 2026-07-10) and one calibration labels file, not PSG. A synthetic data generator is the right MVP for the offline pipeline test, with the explicit caveat that cross-subject real-data performance is unproven until a labeled dataset is acquired. Brief's Risk Register names 'Domain shift from PSG datasets (central/occipital channels vs frontal)' as the largest expected source of error — this should be called out as a calibration observation, not a normative threshold. The paste's 'Why Random Forest over Deep Learning' rationale conflates JEPA (a WorldModel/ research spike, decoupled per CLAUDE.md) with the EEG pipeline; the rationale is opinionated, not evidence-based, and should be removed from the final schema doc. Generator milestone (2026-07-19): Scripts/generate_synthetic_sleep.py landed. Dirichlet sampling preserves the simplex constraint (relative band powers sum to 1.0 by construction). Non-homogeneous Markov with sine-gated Deep->REM gateway produces a recognizable ~90-min ultradian rhythm. Three-seed smoke test: stage fractions vary substantially across seeds (REM 25.7-38.1% over 8h for seeds 7/42/1) — the pasted base matrix's expected-durations do not pin down a unique hypnogram shape, so a downstream trainer that needs stable fractions should sweep seeds and report mean+/-std, not rely on a single seed. Real-adult target fractions (Wake 5-10%, N1 5-10%, N2/N3 50-60%, REM 20-25%) are best hit with seed 7; the other seeds over-REM. Trainer milestone 2 (2026-07-19): Scripts/train_rf_model.py landed. Per the S-3 spec: feature engineering adds wake_rem_ratio and slow_sleep_ratio (per-epoch static) plus per-band rolling-3 mean and t-(t-1) diff (session-bounded temporal context, groupby('session_id') prevents CV leakage). LOSO grid search with LeaveOneGroupOut on N concatenated synthetic sessions. Smoke test (3 seeds, QUICK 2-combo grid, 5.1s wall): per-seed mean macro F1 0.9394 +/- 0.0127, range 0.9297..0.9573 — S-3 success criterion (>=0.6) cleared with massive headroom on synthetic. Top features confirm design intent: wake_rem_ratio #1 (0.132), delta #2 (0.130), alpha/beta/slow_sleep_ratio close behind. Confusion matrix on refit-on-full (optimistic) shows the known hard case is N1<->REM (23 N1->REM and 22 REM->N1 errors per session, matching the brief's known spectral similarity). **Honest framing per research-software-documentation-structure calibration-observation rule:** the high F1 is partly an artifact of training and testing on the same synthetic distribution with no domain shift, no electrode artifacts, no motion artifacts, and no between-subject variability. Real-data cross-subject performance remains unproven. Treat the smoke test as a pipeline-integration check, not as a generalization claim. Full 216-combo grid is opt-in via absence of --quick (estimated wall time: hours on M-series, not run in this session). CoreML export is the next integration step (S-3 milestone 3) and stays held behind the boundary contract.

hypotheses.title: Swift DreamSessionFSM actor (Stage 4, deferred)
hypotheses.question: When Stage 4 evidence gates open, does a Swift `actor DreamSessionFSM` (with `stateHistory` debounce, AASM-aware transition rules, global_policies-driven cooldowns, `Codable HypothesisRegistry` loaded at launch, cascade handlers for on_arousal / on_drift_timeout / on_lucidity_detected) match the Python offline prototype's behavior on recorded EEG, and does it compose cleanly with the existing `Sources/BCIVoice/AVSpeechSynthesizerService` for the TTS cue path?
hypotheses.metric: Replay equivalence: Swift FSM output state transitions over a recorded EEG CSV match the Python offline prototype's output on the same input within tolerance (no transition divergence on N>=20 epochs); BCIVoice composition: TTS cue path completes one full speak/cancel cycle without dropping EEG frames
hypotheses.success_criterion: Replay equivalence >= 95% on stable REM transitions; BCIVoice composition passes a 5-min soak test with no dropped frames

expected_effect_size.replay_equivalence_rate: 0.90-0.99 (debounce + AASM rules are deterministic; small differences expected at boundaries)
expected_effect_size.actor_state_property_bug: The pasted Python FSM's `cascade(to:)` method has a Swift-concurrency bug if ported verbatim: `var updatedFSM = self; _ = updatedFSM.loadHypothesis(...); self.activeHypothesisID = updatedFSM.activeHypothesisID; ...` is a no-op pattern on actor stored properties. Stage 4 implementation must inline mutation in the actor's isolated body.

hypotheses.status_note: Deferred per Stage 3.4/3.5/4 boundary contract (AA6545F1 / EF7BC788 / B4BBC32A). The pasted Swift actor design is the right SHAPE but the concrete type to delegate to is `AVSpeechSynthesizerService` (existing, BCIVoice/), not a fabricated `HypnosisSynthesizer` singleton. The pasted 'iOS app / CoreBluetooth delegate queue / iOS bundle' framing is wrong for this repo — this is a macOS app, EEG comes from BrainFlow, not CoreBluetooth. The pasted Random Forest sketch's 'CoreML for Stage 4 iOS integration' should read 'CoreML for the macOS deployment path matching BCIClassifier's existing ANE-preferred CoreML wrapper.' These framing corrections are recorded in `docs/SleepCycleDesign.md`'s audit section. The pasted `loadHypothesis` accepts the terminal cascade names `abort_to_restorative_sleep` and `trigger_active_confrontation` as string keys — these should be a Swift enum (`enum HypothesisID: String, Codable`) for type safety when the time comes.
